source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

china_plus_one.evidence: Excluding the one-time large HVDC order, the share of exports grew to over 40 per cent of total orders in Q3 FY25, with power quality, substation & renewable orders from Australia, Indonesia, Canada, Croatia, and Azerbaijan, among others. Q4FY25 release: 'Exports and services continue to sustain their growth momentum with significant contributions to the overall order book, with key export orders received from across continents - South Asia, Europe, and Africa.'

govt_capex.evidence: Q4FY25 order commentary: 'Transmission & renewables leading the charge, with an increasing focus on modernizing the grid to ensure reliable supply of green electricity across the country,' followed by industry and rail & metro segments. Company also supplies 765 kV transformers directly to state-owned Power Grid Corporation of India Limited (PGCIL) for national grid expansion, and is investing ~INR 4,000 crore cumulative capex (incl. INR 2,000 crore Karjan, Vadodara large power transformer plant) partly aligned with India's grid-modernization/'Make in India' capex cycle. No explicit % of revenue from government/grid capex disclosed.

rural.evidence: Third-party summaries indicate GSK India maintains a dedicated 'REACH' team tasked with increasing penetration into rural and tier-2/tier-3 markets, and that its distribution network reaches a large majority of pharmacies nationwide; no numeric rural revenue % was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Secondary sources describe standard Ind AS financial-risk-management note language stating the company is exposed to foreign exchange rate risk where transactions or balances are denominated in a currency other than its functional currency, but no primary-source figure or explicit hedging policy for the FY2024-25 report was located.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company description frames Netweb as 'fueling India's digital self-reliance while expanding globally'; export sales (to Middle East, Europe and USA) were ~9% of quarterly revenue with company guidance of 10-11% in the medium term. Risk-factor language notes the company 'depends on a global supply chain for GPUs, memory, networking equipment and other critical components' and that 'geopolitical tensions, logistics disruptions or component shortages could increase risks' -- this is framed as a supply-chain risk to Netweb's own sourcing rather than an explicit China+1 customer-diversification tailwind attributed to revenue growth.

govt_capex.evidence: Third-party research note states 'Government customer/non-government customer revenue mix stood at 59.5%/40.5% in FY25' (an earlier H1 FY25 disclosure had cited ~45.6% government); end-user industries cited include Government entities such as Defence, Education and R&D institutions, plus National Data Centers, IT/ITES and BFSI. Figure is customer-mix based, not a specific 'government capex' line, and was not independently verified against the AR PDF text itself.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company reported to carry minimal debt (long-term debt ~INR 5.7 crore as of Mar-2025) with fund-based bank limit utilisation averaging ~24%; no specific floating-rate share of liabilities was disclosed in sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Netweb is described as 'exposed to INR/USD fluctuations as a net importer of hardware components' and 'undertakes selective forex hedging, though sustained Rupee depreciation could increase procurement costs.' No specific USD revenue or hedged-percentage figure was found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Netweb received a Production Linked Incentive of INR 5,93,97,758 (~INR 5.93-5.94 crore) from MeitY under the IT Hardware PLI Scheme 2.0, for the period July 1, 2023 to March 31, 2024, in recognition of its HPC/enterprise-grade IT hardware manufacturing. No disclosure was found expressing this incentive as a percentage of total revenue.

rural.evidence: Company has pan-India sales network reaching over 60,000 retail outlets with emphasis on semi-urban and rural penetration; regular (mass/affordable) segment volumes grew 79.6% in a recent quarter after nine quarters of de-growth, reflecting rural/semi-urban demand recovery. Industry growth attributed partly to rising rural incomes and conversion from illicit/toddy to IMFL.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key raw materials are ENA (extra neutral alcohol), grain and packaging (glass, PET, cartons). Management commentary notes grain, ENA and glass cost volatility pressuring gross margins; glass bottle costs reported up ~20% and paper cartons nearly 100% due to geopolitical disruptions affecting energy and freight costs, indicating indirect crude/energy-linked packaging cost exposure, though no explicit % of raw material cost tied to crude oil was disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Radico Khaitan exports to 85+ countries across 6 continents including Travel Retail, with key international markets in the US, Canada, Europe and Southeast Asia (brands Rampur, Jaisalmer); overseas markets contribute roughly 8-9% of total sales value. No specific USD revenue % or hedging policy details were found in available sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: Secondary-source reporting (not a direct AR quote): company leadership describes 'exports to NATO' and expanding into North America and EU markets alongside traditional Middle East/Africa/CIS markets, and a $100 million US export revenue target within three years -- export-momentum and market-diversification narrative present, but no explicit 'China+1' framing was found in available sources.

govt_capex.evidence: Secondary-source reporting indicates FY2024-25 was described as Zen's 'highest-ever revenue and order book, powered by large-scale procurement of anti-drone systems, tank gunnery simulators, and live fire range equipment by the Indian Armed Forces' -- domestic revenue is understood to be overwhelmingly Indian government/defense-ministry procurement, but no precise disclosed percentage was located.

pli_scheme.evidence: Company (Acutaas Chemicals, formerly Ami Organics) received formal approval under the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) for its Electrolyte Additives manufacturing project at Jhagadia, Gujarat, with total project outlay of ₹256.47 crore, of which ₹119.12 crore is eligible for up to 25% subsidy incentives till FY2030-31.

rural.evidence: FY25 press coverage of results (citing management commentary) notes Endurance's India business grew Total Income 12.5% vs SIAM industry growth of 11.1% for two-wheelers and 9.2% for all vehicles, and cites 'forecasts of a favourable monsoon, strong demand for replacement and government support for electric vehicles' as positive demand drivers for the sector; no explicit rural-specific revenue percentage disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Company commentary (quarterly result updates) identifies aluminium, steel, copper, rubber and oils/fuels (diesel, PNG, LPG) as key commodity inputs subject to price inflation; raw material cost was reported at 64.8% of total income in Q1 FY26 and 68.4% in Q1 FY27 (quarterly, not FY24-25 annual disclosure); no exact FY24-25 annual raw-material-to-revenue percentage or crude-linked-specific breakout could be confirmed from accessible sources.

inr_exposure.evidence: Endurance derives ~23.6% of consolidated FY25 revenue from its European subsidiaries (Endurance Overseas, Italy, etc.), which is Euro-denominated operating revenue from local manufacturing rather than USD export sales from India; no specific USD-revenue percentage or hedging policy disclosure could be confirmed from accessible sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: Secondary-source analyst coverage (MNCL initiating coverage, Oct 2025) describes TDPS as 'well-placed to benefit from global supply chain shifts, as many OEMs prefer sourcing from non-Chinese suppliers,' positioning it as a reliable, cost-competitive alternative particularly in Europe and the Middle East, with export orders rising accordingly.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports (largely invoiced in foreign currency, per third-party summaries) accounted for ~63% of FY25 sales revenue (Rs 1,278.76 cr total revenue from operations, up 27.8% YoY from Rs 1,000.52 cr in FY24), and ~67-68% of order inflow/order book for FY2024-25 and FY2025-26 per broker/media summaries. No explicit hedging policy or exact USD-denominated revenue % was found in accessible sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: Third-party summary of company commentary (not a verbatim AR quote): 'The company is actively benefiting from the China+1 diversification trend. Major drugmakers are diversifying their supply chain to limit their reliance on China. Divi's maintains supply resilience via diversified raw-material sourcing with reduced China dependence and solvent recovery systems that lower input costs.'

crude_exposure.evidence: Third-party earnings summary: 'Material consumption reduced to 36.3% of sales revenue (from 39.8% year-over-year)... Elevated solvent costs and raw material price volatility, exacerbated by geopolitical tensions in West Asia, are impacting input costs.'

inr_exposure.evidence: Third-party earnings summary noted forex gains/losses (e.g. 'net Forex loss of INR7 crore in Q1 FY27 compared to a gain of INR39 crore in the prior year') indicating some transactional FX exposure, but no explicit hedging policy or USD-revenue percentage was found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Secondary-source commentary attributed to ABB India's FY2024 results/MD&A: 'Revenue growth aided by improved pricing power, higher share of services and exports, localization, and better control over supply chain costs' and 'Diversified revenue streams, including exports and domestic market expansion, ensure steady cash flows.' Analyst commentary (Motilal Oswal): 'Export contribution from ABB continues to rise, peaking in CY24, supported by increasing global integration.'

govt_capex.evidence: Secondary-source MD&A commentary: 'Proactive investment in high-growth sectors such as data centers, renewables and automation, while leveraging opportunities in infrastructure, energy and industrial capex.' Also: 'beneficiary of government capex investments in mega infrastructure and renewable projects' and 'Higher capex in infrastructure, railways, renewables, power distribution, water, energy, commercial buildings, and metals are likely to provide necessary opportunities for growth.'

Company is a defence/aerospace electronics systems provider whose principal customers are Indian government/PSU defence entities. Third-party research (not the AR itself) cites MoD contributing 31% and DRDO 32% of FY23 revenue (~63% combined), with additional revenue from BEL, BHEL, HAL, ECIL and ISRO. FY25 order book stood at Rs 730 crore (Rs 860 crore including negotiated-but-unfinalized orders), of which international orders were a small minority (~Rs 107 crore, ~15%), implying the large majority of revenue/orders is domestic government-linked.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 international/export order book was reported at approximately Rs 107 crore against a total order book of Rs 730 crore; company achieved an export milestone of transportable precision approach radars to a European country in FY24-25.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company commentary describes overseas expansion (plants in Indonesia, Vietnam, Germany, Spain, Mexico; 76 plants globally) and a stated goal of doubling export revenues as a buffer against domestic fluctuations, with JV/technical partnerships spanning Japan, South Korea, Germany and China. No explicit 'China+1' framing tied to revenue growth was found.

rural.evidence: Two-wheeler segment (~45% of revenue) commentary attributes growth to 'resilient rural mobility demand,' citing motorcycle growth (~10%) supported by rural and semi-urban demand and improving rural incomes post-monsoon.

crude_exposure.evidence: Broker/press commentary notes aluminum and plastic resin (crude-linked) input cost increases are 'largely passed through to end customers, resulting in minimal impact on gross margins,' but no raw-material cost composition percentage was disclosed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Uno Minda is listed among certified/approved component suppliers under India's PLI Scheme for Automobile and Auto Components. Only a small number of applicants had received disbursements as of FY25/26; Uno Minda expected to begin receiving incentives from FY27.

china_plus_one.evidence: Rising preference for Indian fluorochemical suppliers amid 'China+1' sentiment benefits NFIL's export-led business; company has started receiving new enquiries from customers seeking supply-chain diversification out of China, and is building a domestic (non-China) supply chain in India for products destined for the US, targeting 70-80% local production within one to two years. Backward integration via a 25% JV in India's only fluorspar beneficiation company also aims to reduce China-linked raw-material dependence.

crude_exposure.evidence: Raw material/cost-of-materials expense was roughly 44% of FY25 revenue (~Rs 1,038.6 cr on ~Rs 2,349.4 cr revenue), with HF (hydrofluoric acid) as the primary input across all three segments plus chloromethane-linked feedstocks; no disclosed split of crude/petrochemical-linked vs. non-crude-linked raw materials was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Company is export-driven (exports ~56% of FY25 revenue per secondary sources; CDMO segment alone reported as ~98% export-oriented in later quarters), implying material USD revenue exposure, but no explicit USD-revenue percentage or forex hedging policy statement was located.

pli_scheme.evidence: No confirmed PLI scheme participation found; a PLI scheme for the specialty chemicals sector was described as still under discussion/not yet operational as of FY25.

rural.evidence: Company commentary describes an extensive pan-India distribution network reaching both urban and rural markets, and heavy premiumization focus: Prestige & Above (P&A) segment accounted for ~89% of net sales in FY2024-25 (up from 87% in FY2023-24), contributing ~83% of volumes. No explicit rural-specific revenue percentage was disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Third-party/broker commentary indicates ENA (agri-based, not crude-linked) is roughly 40% of raw material costs, while packaging inputs (glass bottles, PET resin/caps, paper cartons) saw significant inflation (glass +11-17%, PET resin +30-50%, caps +15-20%, cartons ~100%). No disclosed % of raw materials specifically classified as crude-oil-linked.

inr_exposure.evidence: USL exports products to over 37 countries (Scotch whisky and IMFL brands), but no disclosed percentage of USD-denominated revenue or explicit hedging policy was found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Third-party analyst commentary: "The Indian forging industry is currently benefiting from the 'China+1' strategy, with global OEMs looking for integrated forging and machining partners." Company has been winning new international/European orders (e.g. an international order with peak annual revenue potential of Rs 160 crore, and a ~Rs160 Cr European industrial order), consistent with export-diversification momentum.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Reported via secondary source as managed through a mix of pass-through arrangements and long-term hedging.
inr_exposure.evidence: Secondary-source summary: "Forex exposure at Happy Forgings is handled via pass-through and long-term hedging... raw material pricing, particularly steel, is managed through pass-through mechanisms with a lag, while scrap prices directly impact EBITDA."

china_plus_one.evidence: HAL's export business is limited to helicopter/aircraft sales and services to friendly nations (Nepal, Mauritius, Suriname, Maldives, and historically Ecuador and Israel) rather than commercial supply-chain diversification; exports are reported as under 5% of revenue with no China+1 or supply-chain-diversification framing found.

govt_capex.evidence: HAL is described as 'heavily reliant on the MoD, with limited diversification.' FY25 saw new manufacturing contracts from MoD worth Rs 1,02,000 crore and repair & overhaul contracts worth Rs 17,500 crore, plus a Rs 62,777 crore contract for 156 LCH Prachand helicopters. Company order book stood at approximately Rs 2.55 lakh crore, almost entirely from Indian defense forces, aligned with Aatmanirbhar Bharat/Make in India indigenisation mandate (65% indigenisation in the 97 LCA Tejas Mk1A tender worth ~Rs 65,000 crore).

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue is reported as under 5% of total revenue, implying limited direct INR/USD exposure, but no explicit hedging policy or USD revenue percentage was found.

govt_capex.evidence: EIL is a Navratna CPSE under the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas; its order book and revenue growth are described as driven by capex announcements from PSU oil marketing companies (IOCL, BPCL, HPCL) for refinery expansion, petrochemicals and green hydrogen projects. FY25 order book reached an all-time high of ~Rs 11,700 crore (+50% YoY) on order inflows of Rs 8,214 crore, with consultancy (higher-margin, largely domestic hydrocarbon/PSU-linked work) at ~65-70% of backlog.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company is reported as carrying minimal/no borrowings ("almost debt free"), implying low floating-rate liability exposure, but no explicit AR disclosure of floating-rate liability percentage was located.

crude_exposure.evidence: EIL is an engineering consultancy/EPC services provider, not a manufacturer, so it has no direct raw-material crude exposure; exposure is indirect via client capex cycles — PSU refiners' investment decisions in refinery/petrochemical expansion are influenced by crude price and hydrocarbon sector outlook, which in turn drives EIL's order inflows.

inr_exposure.evidence: EIL has an overseas engineering office in Abu Dhabi serving Middle East/UAE clients (including ADNOC group) and Africa/South East Asia; overseas order pipeline discussion cited a ~40% overseas / 60% domestic split at one point, but no explicit USD-denominated revenue percentage or hedging policy was disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Natural hedge: company offsets foreign currency payables (trade obligations, loans) against foreign currency receivables to manage forex exposure; no separate USD-only breakdown found.
inr_exposure.evidence: International/export revenue (Europe, Canada, Emerging Markets combined) was over 54% of FY25 total sales of ~INR 7,902 crore, per company results commentary; precise USD-denominated share not disclosed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Emcure Pharmaceuticals was among domestic pharma companies approved under Group B of the Government of India's PLI Scheme for Bulk Drugs/APIs (Key Starting Materials, Drug Intermediates and APIs), alongside Biocon, MSN Labs, Wockhardt and others; revenue contribution from PLI-linked products not separately disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: "With the increasing demand from global procurement agencies for supply diversification, Cupid's entry into nitrile female condom manufacturing represents a significant strategic opportunity" (company press release on Nitrile Female Condom development, branded "Made in India" with "Japanese Quality"); FY25 order wins cited from UNFPA, Government of Tanzania, Abafazi Healthcare (South Africa), and Star Pharma (Brazil) reflect institutional buyers diversifying procurement across new suppliers/geographies. No explicit 'China+1' phrase was found.

govt_capex.evidence: FY25 order wins described as 'over Rs 75 crore in high-value tenders from global institutions,' including UNFPA (Rs 18.20 Cr), Government of Tanzania (Rs 14.91 Cr in Jan 2025 and Rs 42 Cr in Feb 2025), and Abafazi Healthcare/UNFPA/Star Pharma Brazil orders (Rs 13.90 Cr combined) plus a Brazil commercial deal (Rs 23.07 Cr for 5.9 million female condoms). No explicit % of total revenue from government/institutional tenders was disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Historic company profile describes ~90% of revenue as export-derived, though FY25-specific mix reported elsewhere as 52% export / 48% domestic following growth of the domestic FMCG/consumer business (Style Baazar-linked retail expansion). Global institutional tenders (UNFPA/WHO/PFSCM, African and Latin American government health ministries) are typically USD-denominated, implying meaningful USD exposure, but no explicit USD-revenue % or hedging policy was found.
